title: Restructure lint pipeline and add dry-run release prober
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Our lint/test feedback loop has grown slow and coupled to monolithic workflows. This PR splits the lint pipeline into modular executors (fast vs. full), introduces a fast 'dry-run' release prober that validates release artifacts without publishing, and standardizes the Go-based CI entrypoint used by multiple repos. The goals are: 1) speed up PR feedback for common edits, 2) make full lint/test runs deterministic and cacheable, 3) provide a preflight 'release dry-run' check that catches packaging/manifest/semantic-version regressions before any publish step.

What changed (high level): - Introduced ci/actions/lint-orchestrator.yml which dispatches to two lanes: fast-lint and full-lint. Fast-lint performs staged checks (tsc, gofmt, basic go vet) and runs only on changed packages. Full-lint runs full unit/integration suites and end-to-end static analyzers. - Added packages/ci/exec-runner: small Go binary used as a hermetic CI entrypoint to standardize environment setup, caching hints, and exit codes across runners. Replaces ad-hoc shell logic in several workflows. - Added tools/release/prober/dryrun.go (+ README) implementing a repository-aware dry-run that: validates release manifest, computes artifact hashes, simulates publishing to internal staging storage without side-effects, and reports a machine-readable report (json) to the CI log. - Updated scripts/ci/run_lint.sh -> now a thin wrapper that calls the Go exec-runner. Kept the shell wrapper to preserve dev local-run ergonomics. - Added lightweight caching strategy and path-aware warmup for node_modules and Go modcache in workflows. - Small housekeeping: pinned a handful of GH Action versions, bumped setup-go to 1.22 action to reduce flakiness.

Testing and rollout: - Iterative verification performed on staging by landing a draft in the redwood-internal:staging branch. - CI flakiness observed on first run (integration shard) due to an environment variable mismatch; fixed in commit 4 by adding explicit BUILD_ENV in orchestrator. - All tests green on final run and reviewers approved.

Checklist: - [x] Fast-lint lane implemented and tested locally - [x] Full-lint lane implemented and smoke tested on staging - [x] Dry-run prober covers manifests and artifact hashing - [x] Exec-runner binary cross-built for linux/amd64 - [x] Workflows updated and pinned action versions - [x] Documentation: tools/release/prober/README.md and ci/README.md updated

Rollout plan: Gradually enable fast-lint on low-traffic repos first (redwood-examples, redwood-sdk-typescript) then flip on core redwood once we observe stable cache hit rates. Dry-run prober will be wired into the release pipeline as a gated required check for release branches.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the old shell wrappers to avoid breaking local dev flows; long-term we plan to deprecate them with an opt-in migration guide in ENG-1180.
commit_summaries: Introduce lint-orchestrator workflow and fast/full lanes
Add packages/ci/exec-runner Go binary and tests
Implement tools/release/prober dry-run logic and report schema
Wire exec-runner into existing lint scripts and update docs
Pin GH Actions and add cache warmup for node/go modules
Fix environment mismatch in orchestrator (BUILD_ENV) after CI failure
review_comments: Liam Chen: Can we add a quick timeout guard around the dry-run artifact upload simulation? If a registry SDK blocks it could stall CI. — addressed (added 30s timeout on the simulated upload).
Marina Volkova: The exec-runner binary looks good; please add clearer exit codes in README for consumers. — replied: updated README and added exit code table in commit 3.
Devon Price: Suggest splitting the node cache warmup to avoid invalidating shared runners; consider warming only for changed paths. — addressed by path-aware warmup change in workflow yaml.
Liam Chen: Observed flake on integration shard on first CI run; stacktrace pointed to missing BUILD_ENV variable. — fixed in commit 6 and re-run CI.
Marina Volkova: Approved after CI green and documentation updates.
merge_outcome: merged via squash after CI green and approvals
release_notes: Modularize lint pipelines into fast/full lanes for faster PR feedback, add a dry-run release prober that validates release artifacts without publishing, and introduce a hermetic Go exec-runner for CI entrypoints. Improves feedback latency and release safety.
conversation_summary: Small refactor that splits lint jobs, adds a dry-run prober, and unifies CI entrypoints; required one CI fix for an env var and small security/timeouts tweaks before merge.
